Amazon.Levels: one — child → “a single, non-sellable parent product”.

Shopify.Cap / mechanism: “There is no ‘no variant’ state” — a standalone product carries the synthesized Title / Default Title.

Walmart.Levels: one — “An item can belong to only one variant group.”

Shopee.Levels: one for the family (item → model, max 2 axes) — but the axis vocabulary nests: variation → variation_group → variation_option.
Shopee.Cap / mechanism: “If there are two levels of variations under this category, variation_group_id must be passed.”

Tokopedia.Levels: one (product → SKUs); a product_families[] object exists above the product, “Applicable only for US local sellers” — unread.

Salesforce B2C.Cap / mechanism: “A variation group is a subset of variations that are part of a base product … can include only one value of a variation attribute.” Beta-gated: “Variation groups will not be created and a warning will be logged if the Variation Groups (Beta) feature is disabled.”
Salesforce B2C.Stated reason: an addressable subset (“all the red ones”); cost: “disables slicing … when variation groups exist for a base product.”

Akeneo.Cap / mechanism: “It should be equal to 1 or 2. If you specify the level 2, you have to specify the level 1 as well.”; levels attribute-disjoint.
Akeneo.Stated reason: content placement: “The attributes that vary by color (variant level 1) are the composition and the pictures. Finally, the attributes that differ by color and size (variant level 2) are the EAN, the SKU, and the weight.”

WooCommerce.Cap / mechanism: a non-product parent is reset to 0.

commercetools.Levels: one in both models — Classic embeds variants in ProductData; Modular Variant --1..1--> Product.

Magento.Levels: one — catalog_product_super_link (product_id, parent_id); a child may hang off several parents.
